_meta.purpose: FROZEN hand-labeled macro-direction extension of the phase3_derisk frozen study set (MACRO_SURPRISE_PREREG.md deliverable). Each snippet is a REAL macro_release print (CPI m/m headline, or NFP headline) from the cloned Track-2 corpus at .bigtmp/track2/units/<unit>/text/<file>. The gold `direction` is the RELEASED-vs-PRIOR (or released-vs-recent-trend) direction, hand-assigned per the rubric BELOW, BEFORE the macro_surprise mechanism was built or measured (PREREG-then-measure: labels frozen before H-M1 runs).
_meta.label_rubric: Direction = the forecast-relevant rate-band move implied by the NUMERIC SURPRISE of the print, from a forecaster's seat. The surprise is released-value vs EXPECTATION, where expectation = the print's OWN stated prior ('after rising Y percent' / 'after being unchanged' / 'the same increase as in May') when present, else the series' recent trend. Which SIGN of surprise is hawkish is the series' causal semantics (taught as the MacroSurpriseSign codebook): CPI ABOVE prior/trend = hotter inflation = hawkish = rates band UP (up); CPI BELOW = cooler = dovish = DOWN (down); EQUAL to prior = no surprise = none. NFP ABOVE prior/trend = stronger labor = hawkish = up; BELOW = weaker = down. The MONTH-OVER-MONTH (m/m) print is the load-bearing surprise vs the m/m prior; the 12-month figure is used only where that is the print's own headline framing (s03). Anchored on the number direction, NOT on any policy verb.
_meta.labeller: macro-surprise prereg (single annotator; labels frozen before build/measure)
_meta.note_on_s03_s52: s03 and s52 are the two macro_release snippets ALREADY present in phase3_derisk/study_set.json (both gold=up there). They are re-stated here for the macro-direction measurement; their gold is identical (released above prior -> up). The remaining 15 are the frozen EXTENSION.

snippets.text: The all items index rose 2.7 percent for the 12 months ending November, after rising 2.6 percent over the 12 months ending October.
snippets.note: CPI 12-mo reaccelerating 2.6->2.7 = above prior = hotter inflation = hawkish -> up. (== study_set s03)

snippets.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) rose 0.6 percent in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, after increasing 0.2 percent in July, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.
snippets.note: Hot CPI 0.6 m/m vs 0.2 prior = above = hawkish -> up. (== study_set s52)
